# The three-valued X < Y of balls, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_less_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The three-valued answer to whether $x < y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, $X$ and $Y$ not being empty, $X$ the ball of center $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$ and radius $r_x$ and $Y$ the ball of center $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$ and radius $r_y$: *yes* only if it holds for every choice of members, *no* only if it fails for every choice, otherwise *unknown*, both masks false:

$$\mathit{yes} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x < y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y, \qquad \mathit{no} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x < y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c_x = c_{x0} + c_{x1}$, $c_y = c_{y0} + c_{y1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `less(X, Y)` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `Ball<T, 2>` | `Trit` | rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `greater(Y, X)` | `Ball<T, 2>`, `Ball<T, 2>` | `Trit` | the operands exchanged; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X$, of center $c_x$ and radius $r_x$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- $Y$, of center $c_y$ and radius $r_y$, is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{yes}$ is true only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x < y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; $\mathit{no}$ only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x < y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; never both. Both false is the answer *unknown*.
- An empty operand gives *unknown*, and so does the whole line.
- When an operand is the empty set or the whole line, the answer is exact: each mask is true exactly when its relation holds.
- For finite operands the answer may be *unknown* although one of the relations holds, close to where it stops holding: certain, not exact.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_less_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallCompare2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallCompare2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_less_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_less_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** a bound of the sum of the radii by radd and bounds of the difference of the centers by add_ball_2_2, compared (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_less_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_less_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`add_ball_2_2`](add_ball_2_2.md), [`radd`](radd.md), [`to_down_2`](to_down_2.md), [`add_up_1`](add_up_1.md), [`to_up_2`](to_up_2.md).

```
# The three-valued X < Y of balls with 2-limb centers (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface",
# "Comparisons": certain): with (z, e) = add_ball_2_2(c_y, -c_x), so that d = c_y - c_x is within e
# of z, and s = radd(r_x, r_y) at least r_x + r_y: yes when s < dl, dl = RD(to_down_2(z) - e) a
# finite lower bound of d; no when s <= ml, ml = RD(-to_up_2(z) - e) a lower bound of -d, s and ml
# finite. Each rounding down of a difference with e is written as minus the rounding up of the
# opposite (dl = -add_up_1(e, -to_down_2(z)), ml = -add_up_1(to_up_2(z), e)), so that the radius e,
# a fused result, is not negated (a rule of the generator). Each implies its relation; never both.
# Both false for an empty operand (a NaN compares false) and for the whole line (s = +inf). Certain,
# not exact: undecided within about e and a step of T at r_x + r_y of the boundary, and when a bound
# overflows.

ncx0        = neg(cx0)
ncx1        = neg(cx1)
(z0, z1, e) = add_ball_2_2(cy0, cy1, ncx0, ncx1)
s           = radd(rx, ry)
sa          = abs(s)
fs          = lt(sa, const inf)
zd          = to_down_2(z0, z1)
nzd         = neg(zd)
tl          = add_up_1(e, nzd)
dl          = neg(tl)
la          = abs(dl)
fl          = lt(la, const inf)
zu          = to_up_2(z0, z1)
tm          = add_up_1(zu, e)
ml          = neg(tm)
ma          = abs(ml)
fm          = lt(ma, const inf)
a           = lt(s, dl)
yes         = and(a, fl)
b           = le(s, ml)
bs          = and(b, fs)
no          = and(bs, fm)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_less_2)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 3 domains of 3 formats | 10 692 716 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
